headline: AI, security, cloud and data are where hiring is concentrating, while general software roles are more selective.

themes.title: AI roles lead the growth lists
themes.text: Reports summarising LinkedIn's Jobs on the Rise 2026 for India put AI and GenAI roles at the top of the fastest-growing categories.

themes.title: Employers screen for LLM, RAG and agent skills
themes.text: Recruiter search data points to LLM experience, AI agents and retrieval-augmented generation as the most requested AI skills, ahead of the classic ML stack.

themes.title: Cybersecurity demand is regulation-driven
themes.text: Security hiring is rising fast, helped by RBI and SEBI rules and the Digital Personal Data Protection Act.

themes.title: Hiring is concentrating, not collapsing
themes.text: Traditional IT hiring has slowed in places, while AI, data, cloud, cybersecurity and product engineering stay strong. Fewer fresher openings means projects and hands-on work count for more.

themes.title: AI is becoming a skill, not just a job title
themes.text: Companies are adding AI duties to existing software, product and data roles, so adding one AI skill to your current path helps in many places.

Generative AI Engineer.note: AI and GenAI roles lead the fastest-growing lists for India in 2026.

Agentic AI Developer.note: Agent building is named a defining 2026 trend, and recruiters screen for it.

Machine Learning Engineer.note: AI/ML engineering is among the highest-premium specialisms.

NLP Engineer.note: LLM work is being layered onto many language roles.

MLOps Engineer.note: MLOps appears in most lists of in-demand AI skills.

Deep Learning Engineer.note: Steady demand, but employers now ask more about LLM skills than classic deep learning.

AI Research Engineer.note: Strong pay, but few openings and a high bar.

Data Scientist.note: Still listed among India's top in-demand jobs, with more focus on applied and GenAI work.

Data Analyst.note: Frequently listed as a fast-growing entry route in India.

Business Intelligence Analyst.note: Steady demand for dashboard and metrics work.

Data Engineer.note: Data platform roles are rebounding alongside AI.

Analytics Engineer.note: Warehouse modelling skills such as dbt are in demand.

Database Administrator.note: Stable but slower-growing than data engineering.

Cybersecurity Analyst.note: One report calls it India's fastest-growing technical speciality by postings, helped by regulation.

Cloud Engineer.note: Cloud remains one of the five core hiring areas.

DevOps Engineer.note: DevOps stays on every major skills list.

Site Reliability Engineer.note: Platform and reliability engineering command a premium.

Backend Developer.note: Steady demand, with AI integration becoming a plus.

Full Stack Developer.note: Developers who can also add AI features are described as hard to find.

Software Engineer.note: Hiring is selective and favours people with real projects.

QA Automation Engineer.note: Steady demand tied to delivery pipelines.

Flutter Developer.note: Cross-platform skills stay useful for startups.

Engineering Manager.note: Few openings; most come from senior engineers.

Technical Product Manager.note: Product management is described as one of India's fast-growing roles.

UI/UX Designer.note: Steady demand, with more AI-assisted design work.
